title: Atomic Unwind Controller with Causal Signal Gating and Telemetry Anchors
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Problem: Config changes to routing, batching, or KV-cache policies occasionally cause regressions in tail latency and cost. Current rollbacks are: manual, brittle (state desync), or aggressive (full revert) leading to unnecessary disruption. Goals: build an automated, auditable 'unwind' controller that can safely roll back a config change triggered by causal telemetry signals, while reconciling distributed state and minimizing customer impact and token-cost spikes.

Solution overview: The Atomic Unwind Controller (AUC) combines: (1) causal signal gating (only trigger when multiple orthogonal signals cross thresholds), (2) KV-fingerprint ledger to detect and reconcile state divergence before/after apply, (3) time-bucketed telemetry anchors to estimate pre-change behavior and simulate impact, and (4) staged unwind with transactional checkpoints and canary probes. The AUC exposes a policy layer for cost vs fidelity trade-offs and emits a deterministic audit trail for compliance and postmortem.

Why this is different: instead of threshold-only triggers, we gate on causal relationships between cost, latency tail, and output-quality regressions and verify state via lightweight KV fingerprints to avoid blind reverts that leave cached state inconsistent. The controller is designed to be conservative by default and escalate with controlled probing when safe.
acceptance_criteria: AUC can be configured as a per-tenant or global controller and toggled via feature flag
Trigger fires only when at least two independent signal groups cross configured guardrails within the same time window (cost, p99 latency, eval-quality)
Controller runs a pre-unwind state verification using KV-fingerprint ledger and aborts unwind if divergence would worsen state
Unwind completes with transactional checkpoints: pre-apply snapshot -> incremental unwind -> post-checkpoint verification
Post-unwind telemetry returns within 10% of pre-change baseline for cost and latency on canary traffic
Audit log contains a human-readable justification and links to traces/PRs for every automated unwind action
Chaos simulations (synthetic load) demonstrate unwind safety in 90% of test scenarios; remaining 10% have manual review path
plan: Week 1: Define signal-gating policies and telemetry anchors; implement simple gating FSM in feature branch
Week 2: Implement KV-fingerprint ledger and lightweight reconciliation API; instrument on staging
Week 3: Wire AUC to config-apply pipeline with transactional checkpoints; add canary probe harness
Week 4: End-to-end tests, chaos experiments, and internal launch to a single customer segment
Week 5: Iterate on thresholds, add rollback explanations and audit UI hooks in Console
risks: False positives if telemetry anchors are not representative of traffic mix
KV-fingerprint collisions on very large keyspaces (mitigate with probabilistic bloom + sample keys)
Unwind may increase short-term cost if recovery requires cache warmup; need cost dampening policies
Cross-region state reconciliation complexity for Private deployments with eventual consistency
rollout_steps: Step 0: Feature flag off in prod; opt-in in staging tenant
Step 1: Enable telemetry-only mode (detect-only) for 48h and validate alerts
Step 2: Enable soft-unwind (notify + dry-run) for low-impact routes with canary traffic
Step 3: Enable automated unwind with approval TTL and human-notify for high-impact customers
Step 4: Gradually expand policy scope and tune gating thresholds based on signals
